items.title: Sid Davilla Interview, 1969-04-17
items.q: There was a fellow in town that used to be proficient at that, Steve Massey Coat. I don't know what he's doing, if he's dead alive now.

ctx.x: Do you think that there is much difference between the kind of Dixieland jazz that colored people play and the kind of white people playing around in your arms? Any particular time? Well, say in the twenties or thirties when you were starting, were you aware that there was any difference or do you think there's any difference now?

Well, on some instruments I could find that there's a thing that I tried to analyze was a saxophone style that came out in the warms, which was unlike any saxophone style I'd ever heard. Because I was interested in the alto saxophone and I used to listen to these white fellas play, white boys play. And they had a style that they got actually a C melody sound on an alto saxophone. And didn't use a style that required a lot of choice notes. They used a rolling profuse style with a lot of notes. And actually it was…
No, that's true. He doesn't use it. What about, did you think there was any difference in the rhythm sections between colored and white?
